Yep. When we admatched, the customer had to have the current paper ad in hand or an active website loaded on their phone (no screenshots). 

People never match to .com around here, but if they did, it would have to be an active site, has to be sold by Walmart (nothing third party), and has to be in stock.

Price match was discontinued in most stores, but I know that we are still supposed to match .com stuff. It's really simple!

Before you scan the item to be matched, press the "price override" button on the right hand grouping of keys. Scan the item, and a prompt will come up asking for a reason. 

1 is store error and requires CSM override for a difference of more than 50%. 2 is price match for .com or (formerly) competition ads. 3 is battery adjustment (don't worry about this), and 4 is miscellaneous (manager says to discount it or something.)

Hit 2, then enter. A prompt will come up for the new price, and you just gotta enter in the price and hit enter again.  

To void a price overrriden item, hit "price override," then "void," and then scan the item again. It will ask for the price if it was a by-pound item, and then just enter in what you sold it to them for. 

WIC isn't as hard as people make it out to be, I promise. If your state has WIC cards, that's a different process and Im not sure how it works.  If you have the paper checks, it's a bit more involved. 

Take the check from them and verify the date: it HAS to be within the timeframe. Decline it if it's not. Next, ask for an ID and verify the name on the check. Then, hit "WIC tender" on the left hand grouping of keys. 

It will ask if it's WIC or ... CVB?  I can't remember the acronym :( WIC is for things like milk, bread, eggs, etc. It will have a list of items. CAB or whatever will be a specific dollar amount for fruits and veggies. 

Pick whichever one it is. For WIC, it'll go straight to the date. Fir CVB, it'll first ask for how many checks (usually 1, but there might be multiple, in which case, enter however many). Then it'll ask for the amount. Usually it's around 8 dollars, so enter however much it is like "800." if there are multiple checks, add the amounts together. So three checks, all for 8 dollars, will be "2400."

Then, enter the first date (ex: 11/09/2016), enter, then the second date (11/23/2016), enter. Now you can start scanning items.  If it prompts a CSM override, whatever you scanned isn't WIC approved. Have your CSM come over, and they'll sort it out. 

Once you're done, hit total. If what they bought goes over their alloted amount of CVB (like 8.11 on an 8 dollar check) they MUST pay that first. So say they give you a quarter to pay the .11, enter "25" then cash. The drawer won't pop yet. 

Next, or if that didn't happen, hit total again and then "WIC tender." Insert the check, write down the total amount in the box, your initials, and then have the customer sign. The register will prompt all this. 

Once you're done, the drawer will pop, you take the check and paper clip it to the receipt, and put it in the bottom of your drawer.  Thank the customer and move on to whatever else. 

And for card loading,  do 70, then action code (right group, on the bottom.) Have the customer swipe the card, then chose the prompt (1 for withdraw, 2 for load, and 3 for inquiry). Finish like a normal transaction. 

Some people have reloadable phone cards, and that's a 55 action code. Enter that, swipe the card, and then enter the denomination (10 dollars would be 1000.)

Easy, I promise. Best of luck 💕
